rules.condition: A screen presents one decision or step for the user to act on.
rules.outcome: Give that decision exactly one primary action. Every other action on the screen must be visually and verbally subordinate (text link, not a second button of equal weight). Doesn't apply to a checklist's per-item CTAs (SAAS-003) or a legally required consent screen's equal-weight buttons (CONSUMER-007) — those are independent items, not competing actions for one decision.

rules.condition: The flow shows a progress bar, step count, or fraction.
rules.outcome: The indicator must reflect real remaining effort. Never show progress that doesn't move, and never include steps the user can't yet act on in the count.

rules.condition: Any screen except the final confirmation screen.
rules.outcome: Must have a way out: back arrow, X, or skip. A flow with no exit reads as coercive, not confident.

rules.condition: The flow asks the user a personalization question (goal, interest, role, etc.).
rules.outcome: The payoff must visibly appear within one or two screens after the answer is collected. If it won't, cut the question instead of asking it for no reason.

rules.condition: Any word appears on screen, or any layout/spacing/component decision is made.
rules.outcome: Route copy to righter and structure to vois-patterns → vois-components → vois-tokens. Don't draft placeholder copy or eyeball spacing.

rules.condition: Designing onboarding for a SaaS/web product.
rules.outcome: Drop the user into the real product on signup. Use a companion checklist alongside it, never a full-screen wizard that blocks the product, unless the account genuinely cannot function until a step is done (e.g. connecting a payment processor).
Show a fraction (e.g. '1/8 completed') plus a filled progress bar, always visible at the top of the checklist, never buried.
One line: title plus one-sentence benefit-first description, plus a single CTA button per item.
Mark with checkmark or strikethrough but keep the item visible in the list. Never remove completed items from view — visible progress motivates finishing the rest.

rules.condition: Optional or deeper items exist (live trainings, 1:1 onboarding calls, advanced setup).
rules.outcome: Surface these below the core checklist, not inside it. Progressive disclosure, not required steps.
Never gate the product's real functionality behind checklist completion.
One question per screen. Never stack two questions on one screen.

rules.condition: A quiz or onboarding sequence screen.
rules.outcome: Show progress as a thin bar at the top or an explicit step count. Never omit a progress signal from a linear sequence.

rules.condition: Any quiz or sequence screen before the final confirmation.
rules.outcome: Back arrow top-left, X to close or skip top-right. Never remove the exit.

rules.condition: The quiz collects a personalization answer.
rules.outcome: The payoff must visibly appear within one or two screens. If it won't, cut the question — it's friction with no return.

rules.condition: The flow will request a native OS permission (notifications, ad tracking, camera, etc.).
rules.outcome: Show a permission-priming screen explaining the specific benefit before the native OS prompt fires. Never let the OS dialog be the user's first exposure to why.
Always pair the primary paid CTA with a visible, if de-emphasized, non-paying path. State price, billing cadence, and cancellation terms on the same screen as the CTA.

rules.condition: A legally required consent or tracking screen.
rules.outcome: Use plain, equal-weight buttons (Accept All / No Thanks / Manage Preferences). Never disguise the choice as a single option with a small 'manage' link.
